transcript:
Header: 2026-03-31 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jared, Priya (Redwood); Maya, Daniel, Samir (Orchid)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on benchmark deltas vs the baseline provider. Reviewed latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, tuning knobs (KV cache, batching, quantization), and next steps for running 8k token tests and security review.

00:00 Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, real quick agenda 	6 run through last week's numbers, dig into the p99 anomalies, talk tuning steps, and align next actions.
00:18 Maya: Sounds good, thanks. We had a few questions from the infra team after the spreadsheet you sent.
00:25 Priya: Awesome. Quick reminder: baseline provider numbers you shared were with cold KV cache; our runs were warm unless noted, so we'll call that out as we go.
00:40 Daniel: Quick clarification 	6 when you say "baseline provider" is that ProviderX? The CSV labels are a bit ambiguous.
00:46 Jared: Yeah, ProviderX in their managed offering, plus a set of open model runs on-prem. We'll refer to them as baseline for this call.
00:55 Priya: Ok jumping into numbers, slide 1 	6 for 2k context, Redwood hosted p50 is ~85ms, p95 ~160ms, p99 ~210ms. Baseline provider p50 ~120ms, p95 ~230ms, p99 ~340ms. So we're seeing roughly 35-40% improvement at p99.
01:18 Samir: That's promising. Are those numbers for single-concurrency or concurrent sessions?
01:23 Priya: These are measured at concurrency 8, token output rate capped at 20 tokens/s per session to simulate chat workloads. We also ran a throughput sweep 	6 I'll summarize.
01:34 Priya: Throughput: Redwood steady-state tokens/sec per GPU ~5,800 tokens/s for the model we swapped in. Baseline provider measured ~4,300 tokens/s on their configuration. Again, our kernel selection and seq-specific batching helped.
01:48 Daniel: Those are pretty big deltas. How much of that is quantization/compute kernel tuning vs routing/caching?
01:55 Priya: Good question. Roughly a third is quantization and optimized kernels, a third is continuous batching/queueing strategy, and the rest is KV cache warmness and shorter host-to-GPU memcpy on our infra. We do want to be cautious 	6 numbers vary on 4k and 8k sequences.
02:12 Maya: Can you explain the p99 spikes we've been seeing mid-run, especially in the 10-15 minute windows?
02:18 Priya: We looked through the logs 	6 two causes. One, occasional garbage collection on the host when multiple jobs align for a checkpoint write in the baseline tests; second, some requests had cold KV cache because they hit different serve shards. We're addressing the shard affinity to keep KV cache hotter.
02:36 Jared: On the p99 spikes, we also noticed a handful of requests hitting a lower-capacity instance (it was auto-scaled in for CPU-bound ops). We plan a pre-warm on canary to avoid that.
02:46 Samir: For Dedicated, pre-warm sounds good 	6 but what's the cost implication?
02:51 Jared: We'll send a Dedicated vs Hosted delta sheet. Early ballpark: pre-warmed pools add ~12-18% to the monthly commit but reduce tail latency significantly during burst windows.
03:06 Daniel: Regarding the 4k tests you mentioned earlier 	6 do those use KV cache warm? Past CSV seemed to have mixed conditions.
03:12 Priya: The 4k baseline run had a mix; we marked warm vs cold. Action item: I'll re-run pure warm 4k with continuous batching forced and share raw logs 	6 should reduce p99 by another 30-40ms in our estimates.
03:26 Maya: Any difference when using the private deployment (VPC) vs hosted API in these tests? We need comparable numbers for both.
03:32 Priya: For VPC private deployments, raw compute perf is similar but network egress and the customer's VPC transit can add 5-15ms depending on region. We captured that in the "VPC + transit" runs you saw.
03:45 Samir: Security team flagged KMS latency in the flow 	6 do you support an HSM-backed key with async signing to avoid blocking inference?
03:52 Jared: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations. For hotspot signing, we offer a caching token approach so HSM calls aren't on the critical path. We'll schedule a security deep-dive next week.
04:05 Daniel: About throughput 	6 can you expand on batching strategy? Our model is fairly chatty so latency matters more than pure throughput.
04:12 Priya: We use adaptive minibatch windows: small immediate batches for low-latency chat, but if the system detects abundant parallelism it expands batching to maximize throughput. There are knobs: max batch size, latency SLO target, and sequence length heuristics. For Orchid's chat use case, we proposed conservative batching to keep p50 low while still getting throughput benefits.
04:32 Maya: Did you try quantized LLM configs? We have concerns about quality regressions.
04:36 Priya: Yes 	6 we ran 4-bit quantized runs with per-channel scaling. Quality delta was within the evaluation threshold you provided (<=1.5% BLEU-like metric change) for the top-5 prompts. We can run a larger eval set if you want.
04:52 Daniel: Please do run the 200-prompt eval. We'll share the prompt set.
04:56 Priya: Added to action items.
05:00 Jared: Back to p99 	6 we saw consistent 210ms on our side for 2k. One outlier test with cold KV was 420ms, similar to baseline. So keeping KV cache warm and shard affinity fixes most tails.
05:13 Samir: For the 8k test you mentioned earlier, what should we expect?
05:17 Priya: At 8k we expect p50 ~470ms, p95 ~820ms, p99 ~1.1s on Redwood hosted with current config, versus baseline p99 ~1.6-1.8s. But we need to run production-like prompts to confirm.
05:30 Maya: That's acceptable if p99 is closer to 1.1s vs 1.8s. Next, about on-prem private deployment 	6 timeline and audit.
05:38 Jared: Private deployment timeline is dependent on infra readiness. Typically 4-6 weeks for a VPC-managed private control plane and customer infra prep. For air-gapped on-prem it's more custom and can be 8-12 weeks. We'll coordinate with your infra.
05:53 Samir: Any blockers from your side for SOC2 docs or for us to run an internal pen test?
05:57 Jared: No blockers, we'll share SOC2 report and the security questionnaire. We'll also provide a sample pen-test scope for your security team.
06:08 Maya: Can we get the raw logs and p99 traces you mentioned? The CSVs are helpful but we want the per-request traces for a few anomalies.
06:14 Priya: I'll upload the per-request traces to the shared drive and annotate the ones that show KV cold misses and GC pauses. Expect that by Friday.
06:22 Daniel: On the topic of provider lock-in 	6 if we go Dedicated with Redwood, how easy is it to fallback to a baseline model if needed?
06:29 Priya: We support policy-based routing and automatic fallbacks to a compatible model variant. You can route by latency, cost, or region, and we keep model versions pinned. The fallback latency is configurable and we can run disaster scenarios in the POC.
06:44 Maya: Good. Also want to confirm tracing hooks for our APM 	6 can you emit spans that have token-level timing?
06:50 Priya: Yes, we provide per-request traces and token timing. We have integrations or simple webhooks to push traces to your APM.
06:59 Jared: Quick recap of technical asks: Priya will re-run warm 4k and produce p50/p95/p99 csvs and per-request traces; Priya will also run the initial 8k experiment with your prompt set once Daniel shares it; Jared will send cost delta and Dedicated pre-warm notes; security docs will be shared and a security call scheduled.
07:20 Maya: That covers it from our side. One ask 	6 can you include a latency breakdown (network, memcpy, kernel) in the logs?
07:27 Priya: Yes, we can add a simple breakdown in the next upload.
07:32 Jared: Great. Any other questions?
07:35 Samir: No, that's it. Thanks.
07:37 Jared: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items.

End: 2026-03-31 15:45 PDT

Notes/Artifacts referenced: "orchid_poc_week5_benchmarks.csv", "redwood_p99_traces.zip", pricing_delta_dedicated_v_hosted_v1.xlsx (links shared in follow-up email).
